entities.summary: Theodosia of Constantinople was a Christian nun and martyr who lived through and opposed the Byzantine Iconoclasm of the seventh and eighth centuries. Born in unknown circumstances, she became a prominent figure in the Orthodox Church of Constantinople, known for her unwavering dedication to the veneration of icons. Theodosia was arrested and executed in 726 CE, along with 70 other Orthodox believers, for her refusal to renounce the use of icons in worship. Her martyrdom sparked widespread outrage and further solidified the Iconoclastic movement, leading to a period of intense persecution and theological debate within the Orthodox Church. Theodosia's legacy continues to inspire devotion and reverence among Orthodox Christians to this day, as she remains a powerful symbol of faith and resistance in the face of adversity. She is remembered as a saint and a model of courage and conviction, whose impact on the course of Christian history cannot be overstated. The Iconoclastic controversy, in which Theodosia played a central role, also had significant consequences for the development of Eastern Orthodox theology and practice, shaping the contours of the church's liturgical and artistic traditions. Theodosia's story serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring power of faith and the importance of standing firm in the face of adversity. Her martyrdom has been commemorated in numerous accounts, including those of the 8th-century historian John of Damascus, who praised her as a 'glory of the Church' and a 'model of Christian piety'. Theodosia's life and legacy continue to captivate scholars and historians, who see her as a complex and multifaceted figure, embodying both the passion and the conviction that define the human experience.
